title: The top 20 theme parks and water parks in Latin America
summary:
Latin America is home to world-class theme parks and water parks like Six Flags Mexico and Aquaventure in the Bahamas. Via the 2024 TEA/AECOM Theme Index, leading theme parks in Latin America continued to show strong performance in 2024 while many of the top-attended water parks saw low to moderate movement.

With the largest population in Latin America, Brazil maintained its position as the region’s leading theme park and water park market. Guatemala’s theme parks and water parks also delivered exceptionally strong growth, reportedly due to a major increase of post-pandemic domestic and international tourism to the country.

As for Latin America’s water parks, attendance declined from the previous year, but the market is expected to remain stable.

The attendance figures and ranking below come from the 2024 TEA/AECOM Theme Index, which can be downloaded here.

​20. Salitre Mágico, Bogotá, Colombia


Salitre Mágico is the largest theme park in Bogotá, located within the Parque El Salitre recreational complex. It includes around 40 attractions, from roller coasters to family-friendly rides, and hosts seasonal events, live entertainment, and festivals throughout the year.

2022 attendance – 608,000

2023 attendance – 629,000

​19. Parque de la Costa, Buenos Aires, Argentina


Parque de la Costa is Argentina's largest and best known amusement park. Located in the riverside city of Tigre, about 30 km (19 miles) north of downtown Buenos Aires, it opened in 1997 and has become one of the most popular tourist attractions in the Buenos Aires metropolitan area.

Parque de la Costa is home to more than 30 attractions, from thrill rides to family-friendly experiences, as well as live entertainment such as musical performances and seasonal productions.

2022 attendance – 617,000

2023 attendance – 639,000

​18. Piscilago, Bogotá, Colombia


Piscilago is a popular attraction in Colombia. Located near the city of Melgar, it has a water park, a zoo, and conservation areas. The water park features 21 ProSlide water rides, including several of the company’s first in Colombia. Piscilago and ProSlide have worked together on 10 projects spanning a 19-year relationship, establishing the park as a key destination in Latin America.

2022 attendance – 914,000

2023 attendance – 702,000

​17. Magic City, Suzano, Brazil


Located in Suzano, Brazil, Magic City is a water park resort in the São Paulo metropolitan area. The attraction combines a water park, amusement park and nature resort set within 300,000 square metres of Atlantic Forest. Guests at Magic City can relax in natural surroundings and enjoy water attractions and family entertainment.

2022 attendance – 763,000

2023 attendance – 732,000

16. Beach Park, Aquiraz, Brazil


Beach Park, a popular water park and resort, is located on the beach of Porto das Dunas in Aquiraz, Brazil. Covering 170,000 square metres, the resort is home to restaurants, hotels, aquatic attractions and an artificial river that transports overnight guests to the water park.

2022 attendance – 800,000

2023 attendance – 850,000

15. Parque del Café, Montenegro, Colombia


Parque del Café is one of Latin America's most distinctive sites, combining an amusement park with a celebration of Colombia's coffee heritage. Established in 1995 and located in the Coffee Cultural Landscape of Colombia, it provides thrill rides, cultural attractions and coffee experiences across 125 hectares.

2022 attendance – 845,000

2023 attendance – 875,000

14. Thermas de São Pedro, São Pedro, Brazil


Thermas de São Pedro is a popular attraction in Brazil. It features waterslides, family-friendly pools, the largest wave pool in the state of São Paulo, and a huge water playground for children. It also offers entertainment, as well as a small farm and a dinosaur park.

2022 attendance – 867,000

2023 attendance – 900,000

13. Mundo Petapa, Guatemala City, Guatemala


Located in Guatemala City, Mundo Petapa is a top amusement park in Latin America when it comes to attendance. Inaugurated in 1976, the site can accommodate 12,500 daily visitors.

Attractions include the amusement park, a swimming pool, a zoo called La Jungla, and a theatre. A new roller coaster called Relámpago was added to the theme park in 2019. The high-thrill Zamperla ride joined many other Zamperla attractions at Mundo Petapa.

2022 attendance – 912,000

2023 attendance – 1,012,000

12. Xocomil, San Martín Zapotitlán, Guatemala


Xocomil Water Park is the largest water park in Guatemala. The 77,300-square-metre site features attractions and slide towers inspired by Mayan heritage. Rides include swimming pools, wave pools and waterslides.

WhiteWater delivered several aquatic attractions for Xocomil. These include a multi-lane mat racer, a Boomerango, a Super Bowl slide, a looping waterslide, and the world’s first AdrenaLIM Blaster.

2022 attendance – 900,000

2023 attendance – 1,078,000

11. Hacienda Napoles, Medellin, Colombia


Hacienda Napoles is a theme park destination close to Medellin in Colombia that used to be the estate of the late drug baron Pablo Escobar. The site fell into disrepair but was reopened as a visitor attraction in 2007 with an initial investment of $10 million, the Independent reported.

Hacienda Napoles has several areas, one a theme park with coasters and Colombia’s tallest drop tower, another a wildlife sanctuary with hippos and other animals. There are also dinosaur and relaxation zones. The water park features giant cobra and octopus slides, pools, and a waterfall.

2022 attendance – 1,200,000

2023 attendance – 1,096,000

10. Hot Beach, Olímpia, Brazil


Hot Beach Olímpia in Brazil features more than 20 aquatic attractions. These range from thrilling slides to a lazy river. Rides at Hot Beach Olímpia include Tangled, a racing waterslide with four parallel lanes. Operated by Hot Beach Parques & Resorts, the park is part of the Hot Beach Resort, which offers an artificial beach and a hot spring bath.

2022 attendance – 1,066,000

2023 attendance – 1,122,000

9. Mundo Aventura, Bogotá, Colombia


Mundo Aventura is located in the city of Bogotá and opened in 1998. Thrill rides at the park include Sky Coaster, Xtreme, Tropicana, Quantum, Crazy Jump, Ranger, and Air Race. Family-friendly attractions include a carousel, arcades, an aquarium, and bumper cars. Mundo Aventura also provides playgrounds and soft play for children.

2022 attendance – 1,015,000

2023 attendance – 1,131,000

8. Fantasilandia, Santiago, Chile


Fantasilandia has grown in recent years. It opened with just eight attractions in 1978 in the O’Higgins Park in Santiago, Chile and is now one of the most popular parks in Latin America. Roller coasters include Mining Train, Boomerang and Raptor, and family-friendly rides include Bumper Boats and Wild Mouse.

Fantasilandia is moving to a larger site in San Bernardo after being in its current location for almost 50 years. PGAV is heading the master planning and concept development for the relocation of Fantasilandia.

2022 attendance – 1,015,000

2023 attendance – 1,150,000

7. Hopi Hari, Vinhedo, Brazil


Hopi Hari is one of Brazil's best-known theme parks and is located in the city of Vinhedo, about 30 km (19 miles) from Campinas and roughly 70 km (43 miles) from São Paulo. Opened in 1999, the park has been adding new experiences in recent years. In 2026, it introduced Aero Venturi, a 40-metre-tall swing tower attraction.

2022 attendance – 1,039,000

2023 attendance – 1,295,000

6. Hot Park, Caldas Novas, Brazil


Hot Park can be found at the Rio Quente Resort, one of the biggest resorts in Brazil. The water park covers 55,000 square metres and also features an aviary with more than 200 birds. The resort offers other facilities, including F&B.

Located in the Cerrado, Rio Quente has five hotels, as well as F&B facilities, and pools and aquatic attractions. Hot Park provides more than 17 attractions in natural thermal waters. Thrilling rides include AeroBike and Xpirado, while relaxing offerings include a lazy river.

2022 attendance – 1,600,000

2023 attendance – 1,427,000

5. Parque Xcaret, Cancun, Mexico


Parque Xcaret features more than 40 attractions in the jungle, caves and underground rivers of Mexico. These include an aquarium and archaeological sites. The park is owned by Grupo Xcaret, a Mexican company and a pioneer in sustainable tourism. It operates parks and tours in Cancun and the Riviera Maya, including Xcaret, Xplor, Xplor Fuego, Xoximilco, Xenses, Xavage and Xel-Há.

Grupo Xcaret’s parks business began in 1984 when Miguel Quintana Pali bought 12 acres in the Riviera Maya and transformed the land into Xcaret, the original destination.

As well as theme parks, the group provides tours and activities to visit the ancient ruins of Chichén Itzá, Tulum and Cobá.

“We are proud to be considered the first and most important ecologically and socially sustainable tourism company in Mexico,” said Pali. He said Xcaret “connects travellers to the spectacular and unique nature of our surroundings, and that will ultimately result in a better understanding of our heritage and culture”.

2022 attendance – 1,637,000

2023 attendance – 1,580,000

4. Aquaventure at Atlantis Paradise Island, Bahamas


Aquaventure, a tropical water park at Atlantis Paradise Island in the Bahamas, opened in 1994. Aquaventure parks are home to attractions including the Mayan Temple, which features a series of rides and slides. Aquaventure also contains a river ride with waves, rapids, tidal surges, steam and waterfalls, and an exhibit for the park’s cetaceans called Dolphin Cay.

There are three Aquaventure water parks in the world, found in the Bahamas, China and the UAE. In 2025, a California-based real estate development company purchased oceanfront land in Hawaii to build a $2 billion Atlantis resort – the first in the US.

2022 attendance – 1,891,000

2023 attendance – 1,790,000

3. Thermas dos Laranjais, Olímpia, Brazil


Thermas dos Laranjais first opened in 1987 and is home to the largest complex of thrilling waterslides in Brazil. The park is located in the northern part of the state of São Paulo.

Thermas dos Laranjais features more than 60 attractions and over 30 F&B outlets across 300,000 square metres. These include waterslides, surfing facilities, pools, rivers and family-friendly offerings. WhiteWater created a range of aquatic attractions at Thermas dos Laranjais. The park’s latest addition is Gigantic Nations, a 33-meter-tall slide tower that branches off to offer two major new and different raft slide attractions.

2022 attendance – 1,954,000

2023 attendance – 1,850,000

2. Six Flags Mexico, Mexico City, Mexico


Located in the Tlalpan forest and borough in Mexico City, Six Flags Mexico is operated by Six Flags. The park offers attractions such as Supergirl Sky Flight and X-Flight, and the Wonder Woman Coaster. Supergirl Sky Flight is a swing tower ride, while X-Flight is a wing coaster. Both opened in 2015.

Newer additions include CraZanity, the world’s tallest pendulum ride. It features a record height of more than 50 metres and reaches speeds of more than 120 km/h.

In 2026, Six Flags México launched the new Speedway Stunt Coaster, a family-friendly Boomerang roller coaster for all ages. Designed by Vekoma Rides, the coaster features energetic twists, controlled speed and a unique themed environment.

2022 attendance – 2,021,000

2023 attendance – 2,051,000

​1. Beto Carrero World, Penha, Brazil


Beto Carrero World is located in Penha, a municipality in Santa Catarina. It is the biggest amusement park in Latin America, with nine themed areas and more than 100 attractions, including thrill rides, coasters, family-friendly offerings and live shows.

Highlights include a Disney-inspired castle, a zoo with more than 700 animals, a Ferris wheel, and character photo opportunities. In addition, Beto Carrero World offers a visitor train, cable railway, restaurants, cafés and shops.

In 2023, the first-ever Nerf-themed land opened at Beto Carrero World. Nerf Mania is a 14,000-square-metre zone with family-friendly rides, a themed restaurant and a Nerf shop.

“This fully immersive experience really leans into the social, active play lifestyle that Nerf has been known for over its nearly 55-year history, all while encouraging friendly competition between family and friends,” said Matt Proulx, senior vice president of global experiences, partnerships and music at Hasbro.

“This marks the largest investment in Beto Carrero World’s history. It took us 31 years to reach this level of international entertainment standard,” said Alexandre Von Janke Murad, president of the theme park’s board.

2022 attendance – 2,500,000

2023 attendance – 2,500,000

title: Six Flags introduces 'Diablo' IP for new Halloween haunted mazes
summary:
Cedar Point and Kings Dominion are the latest parks to announce a new IP experience for this year's Halloween events.

The haunted maze, called Diablo: The Infernal Path, is inspired by Blizzard Entertainment's Diablo video game franchise.

Designed exclusively for Cedar Point and Kings Dominion, the attraction will immerse guests in a series of eerie environments "infused with ancient power, demonic corruption and fiery horrors".

As guests navigate the haunted maze's "corrupted pathways", they will meet demons including The Butcher, Duriel, Baal, Mephisto, Lilith and Diablo.

See on Instagram

“For 30 years, Diablo has challenged players to descend into the darkness and face the horrors that haunt Sanctuary,” said Gavian Whishaw, vice president and executive producer of Diablo IV.

“Celebrating that milestone by bringing Sanctuary to life at Six Flags feels like a fitting way to mark our anniversary.

"Whether you’re coming face-to-face with The Butcher or descending deeper into the realms of darkness, this is a chance to experience the world of Diablo in a way that’s never been possible before."

Kelly Daugherty, Six Flags’ director of entertainment, said the experience "delivers an unprecedented opportunity for guests to experience the world of Diablo in a completely new way".

Video game IPs for Halloween

"The attraction combines the franchise's legendary demons, dark mythology and intense atmosphere with the immersive scares our guests expect during HalloWeekends and Halloween Haunt," she added.

Elsewhere, a new scare zone inspired by Fortnite's signature Halloween event, 'Fortnitemares', is coming to Halloween Horror Nights at Universal Orlando and Universal Studios Hollywood.

The immersive experience will offer "ever-evolving and high-stakes environments" and "puts a twisted spin on the global video game phenomenon", Universal said.

Diablo: The Infernal Path debuts during this year's HalloWeekends at Cedar Point and Halloween Haunt at Kings Dominion.

Images courtesy of Six Flags

title: SeaWorld San Antonio welcomes seven beluga whales as part of rescue effort
summary:
SeaWorld San Antonio has welcomed seven rescued beluga whales as part of an urgent and unprecedented effort to relocate the animals from Marineland in Canada.

The seven whales join two rescued male belugas who arrived at SeaWorld San Antonio on 21 July as part of the first transport, which included the relocation of four additional whales to the Shedd Aquarium in Chicago.

"Given this is the largest number of belugas being moved at one time, we are so happy that all went well and the second transport of this huge rescue effort is complete,” said Steve Aibel, vice president of animals and conservation at SeaWorld San Antonio, who accompanied both transports.

See on Instagram

"All seven female belugas are now at SeaWorld San Antonio. They are receiving veterinary care, nutrition and attention as they acclimate to their new environment.”

The seven female whales who were chosen to move together in a sub-pod are called Xena, Gemini, Skyla, Meeka, Eve, Neva and Calypso.

They are currently housed in a private habitat away from public view while SeaWorld's animal care staff focus on their transition.

Frankie and Bertie Botts, the two male belugas who arrived three weeks ago, are doing well, SeaWorld San Antonio said.

SeaWorld San Antonio has welcomed seven rescued beluga whales from Marineland in Canada

They are getting to know their trainers and being introduced to the existing belugas at the park at their own pace.

SeaWorld has partnered with several other AZA-accredited organisations to help rescue the whales, including the Shedd Aquarium, Georgia Aquarium, Mystic Aquarium and Oceanogràfic Valéncia.

The collective of participating organisations will continue to coordinate future rescue efforts for the remaining beluga whales, part of a pod of 30 belugas formerly housed at Marineland that faced euthanasia if new homes could not be found.

Images courtesy of SeaWorld

title: ArcVigil launches to provide independent lifecycle assurance for aquarium & marine life attractions
summary:
International aquarium expert Warren Baverstock has introduced ArcVigil, an independent consultancy that assists owners, investors, developers, and operators in creating safer, more robust, and commercially resilient aquarium and marine life attractions.

Modern aquariums are expected to balance animal welfare, conservation, scientific research and education with the need to deliver engaging visitor experiences and operate successfully over the long term.

These requirements can become more complex when projects involve challenging architectural and technical environments.


Meeting these demands requires coordination across multiple disciplines, as well as oversight of how design, engineering and operational decisions work together.

ArcVigil was created to offer independent oversight of aquarium projects, concentrating on evaluating assets from operational, commercial, and animal welfare viewpoints.

​Independent oversight


Founded by Baverstock after over 30 years of global leadership in aquariums and marine life, the consultancy provides independent advisory services, design oversight, and operational support throughout an attraction's lifecycle.

ArcVigil's expertise covers initial vision and concept development, feasibility studies, operational modelling, design review, procurement, construction, commissioning, opening preparation, as well as post-opening optimisation, regulatory compliance, technical due diligence, and operational recovery.


“An aquarium can be architecturally extraordinary and technically sophisticated, yet still inherit operational compromises that remain problematic for decades,” says Baverstock.

“Many of the challenges experienced after opening are designed into a project years earlier. ArcVigil exists to give clients an experienced, independent voice capable of looking beyond individual design packages and protecting the long-term performance of the entire asset.”

Aquarium projects usually include architects, engineers, exhibit designers, life-support specialists, contractors, zoological teams, operators, and commercial advisers. Each contributes essential skills, but their expertise is often split across different disciplines, organisations, and phases of development.

ArcVigil consolidates these perspectives from the client’s side.

Without the need to sell equipment, appoint contractors, or protect individual design packages, the consultancy can assess whether decisions align with the owner’s original vision, animal welfare responsibilities, operational needs, and long-term commercial objectives.

This involves challenging assumptions, validating critical decisions, and ensuring considerations for life-support systems, back-of-house environments, animal care, visitor flow, staffing, maintenance, and commercial operations are addressed early, preventing costly constraints later.

​Aquarium expertise


Baverstock’s career spans leadership roles at the National Marine Aquarium, Burj Al Arab, and Dubai Turtle Rehabilitation Project, followed by major marine development projects in Saudi Arabia for Red Sea Global and Saudi Entertainment Ventures.


He led the client-side concept development and operational planning for Corallium, initially called the Red Sea Marine Life Institute, which blends immersive guest experiences, marine science, conservation, education, and research within a key marine environment.

Additionally, he led the development of a new aquarium concept for SEVEN, emphasising close guest engagement, immersive views, and operational excellence from the start, rather than adding these features later.

Alongside new advancements, ArcVigil assists both existing and underperforming aquariums with operational assessments, welfare and regulatory compliance, infrastructure and life-support system reviews, governance, commercial optimisation, and recovery strategies.

The consultancy also collaborates with investors and asset owners during acquisitions, helping them understand not only the nature of their purchase but also the operational risks, future liabilities, and needed investments to safeguard and enhance the asset.

“For owners and investors, the real question is not simply whether an aquarium can be built,” says Baverstock. “It is whether it can operate safely, deliver meaningful conservation impact, inspire its visitors and remain commercially and operationally resilient for decades.”
